messages.subject: zmax in plot.rf
messages.body_plain:
> I´m wondering if the zmax value can be changed in plot.rf. I have LOD values around 30 for small recombination fractions in my pairwise data.
> I´m using  zmax=30, this can be done?

You can specify zmax in the call to plot.rf. Here's an example:

    library(qtl)
    data(fake.f2)
    fake.f2 <- est.rf(fake.f2)
    plot.rf(fake.f2, zmax=5)
    plot.rf(fake.f2, zmax=6)

karl

messages.subject: Splitting a chromosome into two
messages.body_plain:
> I am looking for R code to split a chromosome.
> My chromosome 2 is too large and it is affecting the view of  the distribution  of other markers on other  chromosomes.
>
> So far I have found these, but not sure it this is right and they are not working.
> > dataCNA$chrom<- splitChromosomes(dataCNA$chrom,dataCNA$maploc) #splits the chromosomes into arms
> > unlist(strsplit("chr2")

The simplest thing would be to use a for loop, calling movemarker() repeatedly.

Here's an example: for the hyper data, say I want to split chr 4 into chr 4a and chr 4b.
>  data(hyper)
>  mnames <- markernames(hyper, chr=4)

>  # names of first half of markers, and their positions
>  firsthalf <- mnames[1:(length(mnames)/2)]
>  pos <- pull.map(hyper)[[4]][firsthalf]
>
>  # move these markers to a chr "4a", at same position as before
>  for(i in 1:length(firsthalf))
>    hyper <- movemarker(hyper, firsthalf[i], "4a", pos[i])

>  # rename chr 4 as chr "4b"
>  names(hyper$geno)[4] <- "4b"

>  # reorder chromosomes
>
>  hyper$geno <- hyper$geno[c(1:3, "4a", "4b", 5:19, "X")]
 karl

messages.subject: Addcovar forced to contain all columns of intcovar
messages.subject_clean: Addcovar forced to contain all columns of intcovar
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to use the R/qtl package to analyze a population of 5 different backcross mouse strains. I would like to use the sex of each mouse as an additive covariate, and the strain of provenience as an interactive covariate.

To this aim, I've created a 4-columns dataframe (A, B, C, D) which indicates whether each individual belongs (1) or not (0) to the A, B, C, D strain. I am not specifying the appartenence to the fifth strain, since these four variables are enough to describe the whole population.

However, when I run the scanone function, it returns the following error message:
Warning message:
In checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar, perm.strata,  :
  addcovar forced to contain all columns of intcovar

The code I'm using is the following:

pop_tot = read.cross(format = "csv", file = "bc5full.csv", na.strings = "NA", genotypes = c("1", "2"))
pop_tot = calc.genoprob(pop_tot)
pop_tot.em = scanone(pop_tot, pheno.col = "RSQ_N", method = "hk", addcovar = dati_backcross[, 9], intcovar = dati_backcross[, 4:7])

Perhaps this is somehow connected with the fact that some markers are not informative in some strains, therefore they have not been genotyped (and are indicated as "NA" in the .csv file).

I would like to share a sample of my data, but I can't since it is proprietary data; however, in case the error is not interpretable with only this information I can try to edit the data a bit and/or publish only a part.

Thank you very much!

Chiara

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Addcovar forced to contain all columns of intcovar
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Addcovar forced to contain all columns of intcovar
messages.body_plain:
Interactive covariates should also be included as additive covariates. scanone looks at the intcovar and addcovar, and if there's a column in intcovar that's not in addcovar, it adds it to addcovar and issues the warning.

You can ignore the warning, or you can make addcovar = (sex, strain) and intcovar = (strain). The results should be the same, but you won't get the warning.

A warning indicates a possible problem that may be ignorable. An error indicates a definite problem; you won't get any results.

karl

messages.body_plain:
> I am writing to inquire about a issue in r/QTL in regards to the genetic map plot which I can't seem to solve. Unfortunately, I have not been able to find a resolution on the internet as well. When I generate my genetic map (e.g. plotMap()), my chromosomes (and numbers) appear out of order. That is instead of running from 1 to 21, it shows 1, 10, 11, 12...19, 2, 21, 3, 4... I have doubled checked my csv file, and everything seems to be in order. Thus, I was wondering there were some ways of correcting the numbering in R. Any help is appreciated.

Try the following:

    chr_numeric <- as.numeric(chrnames(mycross))
    mycross$geno <- mycross$geno[order(chr_numeric)]

karl

messages.subject: Getting Didn't converge! message
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am constructing a genetic map with approximately ~3000 SNP markers. After assigning the linkage groups I noticed  that there are some exceptionally large gaps between markers in some of the linkage groups (e.g. LG 18, please see the attached file). To reduce these gaps I  identified bad markers using "Dropone" function and removed the bad markers using drop.markers function. But when I am trying to re-estimating the genetic map afterwards, I am getting  the "Didn't converge" message.

badmar <- rownames(summary(dropone, lod.column=2))[1:21]
mapthis <- drop.markers(mapthis, badmar)
newmap <- est.map(mapthis, error.prob=0.005)
Warning messages:
1: Didn't converge!
2: Didn't converge!

I thought I am getting this error message due to less number of  iterations. So I increased the iteration numbers to 1,00,000 using the maxit function. But still I am getting the same message.

newmap <- est.map(mapthis, maxit=100000,error.prob=0.005)
Warning message:
Didn't converge!

I have been stacked badly at this  point. Please give some advice about how can I get rid from this.

Many thanks in advance, as usual.

Mehedi

messages.subject: RE: [Rqtl-disc] Getting Didn't converge! message
messages.body_plain:
In my experience, this if almost invariably the result of one or markers near one gap end having rather large recombination fractions (i.e. rf vales exceptionally higher than the theoretical expectation rf<=0.5, or even sampling error range rf <=0.5-0.6 relative to your population number) with one or more markers near the other gap end.  Karl can probably suggest some elegant R code that will help you identify which of your gap-flanking markers are problematic in that regard.

Jim

messages.subject: plotting multiple QTL confidence intervals on plot of genetic map or with LOD curves
messages.subject_clean: plotting multiple QTL confidence intervals on plot of genetic map or with LOD curves
messages.body_plain:
> I was wondering whether there was a way to plot multiple confidence intervals on 4 separate linkage groups found on one graph. To be specific, I have 4 chromosomes on one graph, each possessing a QTL, and I am trying to plot the CI for each one of them. I have used "lines()", but it seems that the CI only shows up for one of the chromosomes and not the other 3.  If I try to add more lines, the latter overlays on top of the former lines. I hope this makes sense.

I would use segments().

Are you trying to plot the CI on the genetic map, or on the plot of the LOD curves?

Here's an example of the former.
data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1)
out <- scanone(hyper)
above3.2 <- summary(out, threshold=3.2)

plot.map(hyper, shift=FALSE)

for(i in 1:nrow(above3.2)) {

    thischr <- above3.2[i,1]
    ci <- lodint(out, chr=thischr)
    lo <- ci[1,2]
    hi <- ci[nrow(ci), 2]
    numchr <- which(chrnames(hyper) == thischr)

    segments(numchr+0.3, lo, numchr+0.3, hi,
             lwd=2, col="violetred")

    segments(numchr+0.2, lo, numchr+0.4, lo,
             lwd=2, col="violetred")

    segments(numchr+0.2, hi, numchr+0.4, hi,
             lwd=2, col="violetred")
}

And here's an example of the latter:

plot(out)
for(i in 1:nrow(above3.2)) {
    thischr <- above3.2[i,1]
    ci <- lodint(out, chr=thischr)
    lo <- ci[1,2]
    hi <- ci[nrow(ci), 2]

    segments(xaxisloc.scanone(out, thischr, lo), 0,
             xaxisloc.scanone(out, thischr, hi), 0, lwd=2, col="violetred")

    segments(xaxisloc.scanone(out, thischr, lo), -0.1,
             xaxisloc.scanone(out, thischr, lo), 0.1, lwd=2, col="violetred")

    segments(xaxisloc.scanone(out, thischr, hi), -0.1,
             xaxisloc.scanone(out, thischr, hi), 0.1, lwd=2, col="violetred")
}

karl

messages.subject: Re: Getting Didn't converge! message
messages.body_plain:
Mehedi,

Looking at your plot it seems that for "chromosomes" 5, 7 and 10 there could be two linkage groups.  For chromosome 19, it could be a few bad markers. My recommendations would be as follows:

(1) Are you sure about the linkage groups ("chromosomes")?  If not, then consider the possibility that there are two linkage groups for some "chromosomes".
(2) Look at the raw data for the markers flanking the gaps.  Pick, say 5 markers on each side.  Make plot.geno() or geno.image().  If needed use a subset of individuals to look carefully.
(3) One possibility is swapped alleles.  That would make 2 cM interval appear to have a recombination fraction exceeding 0.5 (as Jim Sprecht mentioned).

Can you post to us the figure for (3) above for chromosome 5?  Sometimes, looking at the raw data clarifies issues.

Saunak

messages.subject: Re: Getting Didn't converge! message
messages.body_plain:
This large gaps are the problem; if they're real, you might want to split those linkage groups into two.

If you don't get convergence of the estimates, you can use replace.map and then continue from where you left off.

  newmap <- est.map(mapthis, error.prob=0.005, maxit=1e5)
  mapthis <- replace.map(mapthis, newmap)
  newmap <- est.map(mapthis, error.prob=0.005, maxit=1e5)

karl

The problem is solved after removing the problematic individuals with abnormal crossovers. Many thanks for all the support.

(I got the following email and thought I should post it, with the author's permission.)

Question about batch permutations of phenotypes using "perm.strata".

When I run a single trait using this approach, there is no problem. The machinery removes NAs from both the phenotype and the perm.strata vector. Both the cross and the perm.strata vector are culled from 241 individuals to 238 and the perms proceed without a problem.

However, when I batch the phenotypes together, I get an error. It seems that NAs are removed from the phenotype, but not from the perm.strata vector, resulting in different lengths of the arguments, returning an error.

Do you have a work around for this problem? If not, of course I can loop through the phenotypes, but this is significantly slower, especially with scantwo.

messages.body_plain:
There's an example in the help file for effectplot:

### Plot of sex- and genotype-specific phenotype means
mname <- find.marker(fake.f2, 13, 24) # marker D13M254
# sex and a marker
effectplot(fake.f2, mname1=mname, mname2="Sex",
           mark2=sex, geno2=c("F","M"))

# Same as above, switch role of sex and the marker
# sex and marker
effectplot(fake.f2, mname1="Sex", mark1=sex,
           geno1=c("F","M"), mname2=mname)

plotPXG won't take covariates.

karl

messages.subject: Re: plotting multiple QTL confidence intervals on plot of genetic map or with LOD curves
messages.subject_clean: plotting multiple QTL confidence intervals on plot of genetic map or with LOD curves
messages.body_plain:
To plot selected chromosomes, use the chr argument to plot.scanone, and also to xaxisloc.scanone. Here's an example. It's the same as before except the bits with sigchr.

data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1)
out <- scanone(hyper)
above3.2 <- summary(out, threshold=3.2)

sigchr <- above3.2[,1]

plot(out, chr=sigchr)

for(i in 1:nrow(above3.2)) {
    thischr <- above3.2[i,1]
    ci <- lodint(out, chr=thischr)
    lo <- ci[1,2]
    hi <- ci[nrow(ci), 2]

    segments(xaxisloc.scanone(out, thischr, lo, chr=sigchr), 0,
             xaxisloc.scanone(out, thischr, hi, chr=sigchr), 0, lwd=2, col="violetred")

    segments(xaxisloc.scanone(out, thischr, lo, chr=sigchr), -0.1,
             xaxisloc.scanone(out, thischr, lo, chr=sigchr), 0.1, lwd=2, col="violetred")

    segments(xaxisloc.scanone(out, thischr, hi, chr=sigchr), -0.1,
             xaxisloc.scanone(out, thischr, hi, chr=sigchr), 0.1, lwd=2, col="violetred")
}
